_meta.safety: For low-voltage (5 V or less) learning circuits. Not a safety check. Never use on mains wiring.
_meta.note: Keys are the exact class names of the CircuitCoach YOLO26n model. Classes without a card show their name only. References marked checked=false still need to be opened and confirmed.

7-Segment-Display.name: 7-segment display
7-Segment-Display.purpose: Shows digits 0-9 (and a few letters) using seven LED bars, for counters, clocks and timers.
key_facts: Seven segments named a-g plus a decimal point (DP)
Common-cathode type: shared pin to GND; common-anode type: shared pin to +
Multi-digit displays are driven one digit at a time (multiplexing) or with a driver chip
cautions: Each segment is an LED and needs its own current-limiting resistor
cannot_tell: Whether it is common-anode or common-cathode - check the part number or test one segment

Arduino-Mega.name: Arduino Mega 2560
Arduino-Mega.purpose: A large Arduino board with many more pins, for projects with lots of sensors, motors or displays.
key_facts: ATmega2560 microcontroller at 16 MHz, 5 V logic
54 digital pins (15 PWM) and 16 analog inputs
4 hardware serial ports and 256 KB of program memory
cautions: Same per-pin current limits as the Uno - use drivers for motors and relays
cannot_tell: Genuine board or clone

Arduino-Nano.name: Arduino Nano
Arduino-Nano.purpose: A small, breadboard-friendly Arduino with the same chip as the Uno. Plug it straight into a breadboard for compact projects.
key_facts: Classic Nano: ATmega328P at 16 MHz, 5 V logic
14 digital pins (6 PWM) and 8 analog inputs; A6 and A7 are analog-only
Original board uses a mini-USB connector; many clones use a CH340 USB chip that needs a driver
cautions: Same current limits as the Uno: do not drive motors directly from its pins
Nano 33 IoT, Nano 33 BLE and Nano ESP32 look similar but use 3.3 V logic - 5 V signals can damage them
cannot_tell: Whether it is the classic 5 V Nano or a 3.3 V Nano variant
Genuine board or clone

Arduino-Uno.name: Arduino Uno
Arduino-Uno.purpose: A microcontroller board that runs your program (sketch) and reads sensors or drives LEDs, buzzers and other parts. The most common first board for learning.
key_facts: Classic Uno R3: ATmega328P microcontroller at 16 MHz, 5 V logic
14 digital pins (6 can output PWM: 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11) and 6 analog inputs (A0-A5)
Powered by USB, or 7-12 V on the barrel jack / VIN pin
About 20 mA per I/O pin is the safe working limit; 40 mA is the absolute maximum
cautions: Never power motors or several servos from the 5 V pin - use a separate supply and a driver
Always put a resistor in series with an LED on an output pin
Its pins output 5 V: check that 3.3 V modules can accept 5 V signals
cannot_tell: Whether the board is a genuine Arduino or a clone
Which revision it is - newer Uno R4 boards look similar but use a different chip

references.title: Overview of the Arduino UNO components (official)

BJT-Transistor.name: BJT transistor
BJT-Transistor.purpose: A small current into the base controls a larger current through the transistor, so a microcontroller pin can switch an LED strip, buzzer, relay or small motor.
key_facts: Three legs: collector, base and emitter
NPN types (for example BC547, 2N2222, 2N3904) and PNP types (for example BC557, 2N3906)
Use a resistor between the microcontroller pin and the base (around 1 kOhm is a common start)
cautions: Pin order differs between part numbers - read the number on the flat face and check its datasheet
Add a flyback diode when switching motors or relays
cannot_tell: Whether it is NPN or PNP, or its part number
Other parts in the same black 3-leg package (MOSFETs, voltage regulators, temperature sensors) look alike

Bluetooth-Module.name: Bluetooth module (HC-05 / HC-06)
Bluetooth-Module.purpose: Adds a wireless serial link so a phone app can send commands to, or receive data from, your project.
key_facts: Talks to the microcontroller over UART serial (TX/RX)
Default data speed is 9600 baud (HC-05 AT command mode uses 38400)
Uses classic Bluetooth serial: works with Android phone apps; iPhones do not support this profile
cautions: Its RX pin uses 3.3 V logic - use a voltage divider (for example 1 kOhm and 2 kOhm) from a 5 V Arduino's TX
Power the VCC pin from 3.6-6 V (5 V is typical)
cannot_tell: Whether it is an HC-05 or HC-06, or a BLE module that looks similar

Breadboard.name: Breadboard
Breadboard.purpose: A reusable board for building circuits without soldering: push component legs and jumper wires into the holes.
key_facts: Each short row of 5 holes is connected inside; rows on opposite sides of the centre gap are not connected
Chips (ICs) straddle the centre gap so each pin gets its own row
The long + and - rails along the edges carry power; on some long boards the rails are split in the middle
cautions: For low-voltage, low-current circuits only - never mains
Worn contacts cause loose connections; press parts in firmly
cannot_tell: Whether the power rails are split in the middle - check with a multimeter

Buck-Converter.name: Buck converter (step-down module)
Buck-Converter.purpose: Efficiently lowers a higher DC voltage to a lower one - for example from a 12 V battery to 5 V for an Arduino and servos.
key_facts: Common modules use the LM2596 chip (input up to 40 V, up to 3 A); the output voltage is set with the multi-turn trimmer
The input must be a couple of volts higher than the output
Much more efficient than a linear regulator, so it stays cooler
cautions: Set the output with a multimeter before connecting your circuit
Check input and output polarity - many modules have no reverse-polarity protection
cannot_tell: Its current rating or which chip it uses

Buzzer.name: Buzzer
Buzzer.purpose: Makes beeps and tones for alarms, timers and feedback in projects.
key_facts: Active buzzer: has a built-in oscillator and beeps when you simply apply DC (digitalWrite HIGH)
Passive buzzer: needs a changing signal, for example Arduino's tone() function, and can play different notes
Usually polarised: the + leg is often marked and longer
cautions: Connect with the correct polarity
Larger buzzers may need a transistor instead of a direct pin connection
cannot_tell: Whether it is active or passive
Its rated voltage

Capacitor-10mf.name: Electrolytic capacitor (small, labelled 10mf)
Capacitor-10mf.purpose: Stores charge for smoothing, decoupling and simple timing circuits.
key_facts: In this dataset the label most likely means 10 microfarads (uF)
Polarised: the stripe marks the negative (-) leg, which is also shorter
Read the capacitance and voltage rating on the body
cautions: Respect the polarity and the voltage rating
cannot_tell: Its exact capacitance and voltage rating

Capacitor-470mf.name: Electrolytic capacitor (large, labelled 470mf)
Capacitor-470mf.purpose: Stores charge to smooth a power supply and absorb current spikes, for example near motors or on a breadboard's power rails.
key_facts: In this dataset the label most likely means 470 microfarads (uF)
Polarised: the stripe on the side marks the negative (-) leg, which is also shorter
The voltage rating is printed on the can
cautions: Connecting it backwards or above its voltage rating can make it bulge or burst
Large capacitors can stay charged after power is removed
cannot_tell: Its exact capacitance and voltage rating - read the printing

DC-Motor.name: DC motor
DC-Motor.purpose: Spins when connected to DC power; used for wheels, fans and other moving parts.
key_facts: Speed rises with voltage; swapping the two wires reverses the direction
Speed can be controlled with PWM through a driver
Draws much more current when starting or stalled than when running freely
cautions: Never connect it directly to an Arduino pin - use a transistor/MOSFET with a flyback diode, or a motor driver board
Power it from a separate supply, sharing ground with the microcontroller
cannot_tell: Its rated voltage, current or speed

references.title: Motors and Selecting the Right One (SparkFun)

Diode.name: Diode (rectifier)
Diode.purpose: Lets current flow in one direction only. Used to protect circuits from reverse power and to absorb voltage spikes from motors and relays.
key_facts: The band on the body marks the cathode (-) end
A silicon diode drops about 0.6-0.7 V when conducting
Common rectifier diodes such as the 1N4001-1N4007 family have a black body
cautions: Check the direction before powering the circuit
Across a motor or relay coil, the band faces the + supply (flyback diode)
cannot_tell: Its exact part number, current or voltage rating
Whether a small glass diode is a normal diode or a Zener diode

ESP32.name: ESP32 development board
ESP32.purpose: A fast microcontroller with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, used for IoT projects that send data to a phone or the internet.
key_facts: ESP32 chip: dual-core 32-bit Xtensa LX6, up to 240 MHz
Built-in 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (Classic and Low Energy)
Runs at 3.3 V; programmable with the Arduino IDE or Espressif's ESP-IDF
cautions: Its pins are 3.3 V - do not connect 5 V signals directly (use a voltage divider or level shifter)
Wi-Fi causes current spikes: use a good USB cable and supply
Some pins (for example GPIO0, 2, 12, 15) affect booting - avoid them for inputs at first
cannot_tell: Which ESP32 variant it is (ESP32, S2, S3, C3 boards can look alike)
Flash memory size

ESP32-CAM.name: ESP32-CAM
ESP32-CAM.purpose: A small ESP32 board with a camera and microSD slot, used for photo capture, video streaming and simple vision projects.
key_facts: ESP32 chip with a 2 MP OV2640 camera and a microSD card slot (common AI-Thinker board)
The basic board has no USB port: program it through a USB-to-serial adapter (for example an FT232 module) or an ESP32-CAM-MB base board
To upload code, connect GPIO0 to GND and reset the board
cautions: Use 3.3 V logic on the serial pins
A weak power supply causes 'brownout' resets - give it a solid 5 V supply
cannot_tell: The exact board maker or camera version

Gas-Sensor.name: Gas sensor module (MQ series)
Gas-Sensor.purpose: Detects gases such as smoke, LPG, alcohol or air pollutants, depending on the MQ number printed on it - for learning about gas-sensing projects.
key_facts: Contains a heater: the sensor gets warm and draws more current than most sensors
Analog output rises with gas concentration; digital output switches at a threshold set by the trimmer
The MQ number (MQ-2, MQ-3, MQ-135 ...) decides which gases it is most sensitive to
cautions: Let it warm up a few minutes before each reading; a new sensor needs a 24-48 hour first burn-in for stable readings
Not a certified safety or gas-leak detector - never rely on it to protect people
The metal cap gets hot
cannot_tell: Which MQ type it is - read the number on the sensor

Humidity-Sensor.name: Temperature and humidity sensor (DHT11 / DHT22)
Humidity-Sensor.purpose: Measures air temperature and relative humidity - for weather stations, greenhouses and room monitors.
key_facts: One data wire plus power; Arduino library: DHT sensor library
DHT11 (usually blue): 0-50 C (+/-2 C), 20-80 % RH (+/-5 %), one reading per second
DHT22/AM2302 (usually white): -40 to 80 C (+/-0.5 C), 0-100 % RH, one reading every 2 seconds
cautions: Reading faster than the sensor allows returns errors or old values
Bare sensors need a pull-up resistor (about 10 kOhm) on the data pin; most modules already have one
cannot_tell: Whether it is a DHT11 or DHT22 for certain - colour is only a hint

IR-Sensor.name: IR obstacle sensor module
IR-Sensor.purpose: Detects a nearby object by shining infrared light and sensing the reflection - used for obstacle-avoiding robots and object counters.
key_facts: An IR LED and an IR receiver side by side, plus a comparator chip
Digital output: on most modules OUT goes LOW when an object is detected
The blue trimmer sets the detection distance (a few centimetres)
cautions: Sunlight and strong lamps cause false readings
Black or shiny surfaces reflect less IR and may not be detected
cannot_tell: Whether its output is active-LOW or active-HIGH

Keypad.name: Membrane keypad (4x4)
Keypad.purpose: A flat keypad for entering numbers and codes - for password locks, calculators and menus.
key_facts: 16 keys in 4 rows and 4 columns, so it needs 8 pins (a 3x4 keypad needs 7)
The microcontroller scans rows and columns to find the pressed key
Arduino library: Keypad
cautions: Uses many pins - on small boards plan pins before wiring other parts
cannot_tell: The row and column order of the ribbon pins - check the datasheet or test

references.title: 4x3 and 4x4 membrane keypad with Arduino (Last Minute Engineers)

LCD-Display.name: Character LCD (16x2)
LCD-Display.purpose: Shows text and numbers on 2 lines of 16 characters - for sensor readings, menus and messages.
key_facts: Uses the standard HD44780-compatible controller; Arduino library: LiquidCrystal
Wired directly it needs about 6 data/control pins
With an I2C backpack board it needs only SDA and SCL (common addresses 0x27 or 0x3F; library LiquidCrystal_I2C)
cautions: If you see blank boxes or nothing, turn the contrast potentiometer first
cannot_tell: Whether an I2C backpack is fitted on the back, or its I2C address

LDR-Sensor.name: LDR (light-dependent resistor)
LDR-Sensor.purpose: A resistor whose value falls as light increases - used for automatic night lamps and light-level sensing.
key_facts: Bright light: low resistance; darkness: high resistance
Read it with a voltage divider (LDR + fixed resistor, for example 10 kOhm) into an analog pin
Has no polarity - either way round works
cautions: It responds slowly and is not calibrated - use it to compare light levels, not to measure lux
cannot_tell: Its resistance range

LED-Light.name: LED
LED-Light.purpose: A light-emitting diode used as an indicator light or for simple light effects.
key_facts: The longer leg is the anode (+); the flat edge of the rim marks the cathode (-)
Always use a series resistor: R = (supply voltage - LED voltage) / current
Example at 5 V: a red LED (about 2 V) at about 15 mA needs roughly 200 Ohm, so use 220 Ohm
cautions: Without a resistor the LED and the microcontroller pin can be damaged
cannot_tell: Its exact forward voltage or brightness rating

Motion-Sensor.name: PIR motion sensor (HC-SR501)
Motion-Sensor.purpose: Detects movement of people or animals by sensing changes in infrared (body heat) - used for alarms and automatic lights.
key_facts: Powered from about 5 V (4.5-20 V); output is a 3.3 V digital HIGH when motion is detected
Two potentiometers: sensitivity (range up to about 7 m) and how long the output stays HIGH
A jumper selects single or repeat trigger mode
cautions: Wait about 30-60 seconds after power-up before trusting the output
Heaters, sunlight and fans can cause false triggers
cannot_tell: How the potentiometers and jumper are set

Motor-Driver.name: Motor driver module (L298N type)
Motor-Driver.purpose: Lets a microcontroller control the speed and direction of DC motors, which need far more current than a pin can give. The usual choice for two-wheel robot cars.
key_facts: Dual H-bridge: drives 2 DC motors (or 1 stepper) in both directions
About 2 A continuous per channel; motor supply 5-35 V
IN1/IN2 and IN3/IN4 set direction; PWM on ENA/ENB sets speed
Drops about 2 V, so a 12 V supply gives the motors roughly 10 V
cautions: Remove the 5 V regulator jumper if the motor supply is above 12 V, and then supply 5 V logic separately
Connect the driver GND to the microcontroller GND
The heat sink gets hot at high current
cannot_tell: Which driver chip it uses (L298N, L293D and other boards look similar)

references.title: L298N motor driver module with Arduino (Last Minute Engineers)

OLED-Display.name: OLED display (0.96 inch)
OLED-Display.purpose: A small, sharp graphics screen for text, numbers, icons and simple graphs.
key_facts: Common type: 128 x 64 pixels with an SSD1306 controller
4-pin versions use I2C (usually address 0x3C); 6-7 pin versions use SPI
Arduino libraries: Adafruit SSD1306 + Adafruit GFX, or U8g2
cautions: Check VCC: many modules accept 3.3-5 V, but not all
1.3 inch versions often use the SH1106 controller and need a different library setting
cannot_tell: Its controller chip or I2C address

Push-Switch.name: Push button switch
Push-Switch.purpose: A momentary button: connected only while pressed. Used for start, reset and user input.
key_facts: Read it with a digital pin and a pull-up or pull-down resistor
With pinMode(pin, INPUT_PULLUP) the pin reads LOW when the button is pressed
Buttons 'bounce': add a short delay or debounce code
cautions: Without a pull-up or pull-down the input floats and gives random readings
cannot_tell: Its current rating, or which legs are connected inside - check with a multimeter

Relay-Module.name: Relay module
Relay-Module.purpose: An electrically controlled switch: a small signal from the microcontroller turns a separate circuit on or off, with no electrical connection between them.
key_facts: Contacts: COM (common), NO (normally open), NC (normally closed)
The module includes the transistor and flyback diode needed to drive the relay coil
Many modules are active-LOW: writing LOW to IN switches the relay on
cautions: The printed ratings (for example 10 A 250 VAC) are not an invitation: learners should only switch low-voltage loads - never mains
The relay clicks and draws more current than a sensor; power it from 5 V, not a 3.3 V pin
cannot_tell: Its coil voltage or whether it is active-HIGH or active-LOW

references.title: Button and Switch Basics - relays section (SparkFun)

Resistor.name: Resistor
Resistor.purpose: Limits current or sets voltages: protecting LEDs, pulling inputs up or down, and building voltage dividers.
key_facts: Ohm's law: V = I x R
Coloured bands give the value in ohms
Common through-hole resistors are rated 1/4 W
cautions: Check the power rating: too much current makes it hot
cannot_tell: Its value - the app does not read colour bands; use the colour code or a multimeter

Servo-Motor.name: Servo motor (hobby micro servo)
Servo-Motor.purpose: Turns to a set angle and holds it - used for robot arms, steering and pointers.
key_facts: Three wires: brown/black = GND, red = + supply (about 5 V), orange/yellow = control signal
Controlled by a pulse about every 20 ms; the pulse width (about 1-2 ms) sets the angle
Small servos such as the SG90 turn about 180 degrees; use the Arduino Servo library
cautions: Movement causes current spikes: power several servos from a separate 5 V supply with a shared ground
Do not force the horn by hand - the plastic gears strip easily
cannot_tell: Its torque or whether it is a continuous-rotation servo

Soil-Moisture-Sensor.name: Soil moisture sensor
Soil-Moisture-Sensor.purpose: Estimates how wet soil is - for plant-watering and smart-garden projects.
key_facts: Two-pronged probe plus a small comparator board
A0 gives an analog value; D0 switches at a threshold set by the trimmer
Calibrate by reading it in dry soil and in wet soil
cautions: Resistive probes corrode quickly if powered all the time - power them only while reading
Keep the electronics board dry
cannot_tell: Whether it is a resistive or capacitive type for certain

Sonar-Sensor.name: Ultrasonic distance sensor (HC-SR04)
Sonar-Sensor.purpose: Measures distance to an object by sending a sound pulse and timing the echo - used for obstacle-avoiding robots and parking sensors.
key_facts: Pins: VCC, Trig, Echo, GND
Range about 2 cm to 400 cm; start a reading with a 10 microsecond HIGH pulse on Trig
Echo stays HIGH for the round-trip time: distance (cm) = time (microseconds) x 0.0343 / 2
cautions: The classic version outputs 5 V on Echo - use a voltage divider for 3.3 V boards such as the ESP32
Soft, angled or very small objects may not reflect the sound well
cannot_tell: Whether it is the classic 5 V version or a 3.3-5 V version

TCRT5000.name: TCRT5000 reflective sensor
TCRT5000.purpose: A very short-range infrared reflection sensor, mainly used to tell black lines from a white surface in line-following robots.
key_facts: One IR LED and one phototransistor in the same block
Strongest signal about 2.5 mm from the surface; useful range roughly 0.2-15 mm
On modules: D0 gives a digital output (threshold set by the trimmer), A0 gives an analog value
cautions: Mount it at a fixed, short height above the track
Calibrate on your actual line and floor - lighting changes the readings
cannot_tell: Whether it is on a module with a comparator or a bare sensor

Tact-Switch.name: Tactile switch
Tact-Switch.purpose: A small square momentary push button that clicks when pressed - the most common button in Arduino kits.
key_facts: Common size is 6 x 6 mm with 4 legs
The legs are connected in pairs inside; pressing joins the two pairs
Place it across the breadboard's centre gap; use INPUT_PULLUP and debounce like any button
cautions: Rotating it 90 degrees can short the circuit permanently - test which pairs are connected
cannot_tell: Which legs are paired inside - check with a multimeter

Taper-Potentiometer.name: Rotary potentiometer
Taper-Potentiometer.purpose: A knob that changes resistance - used to set brightness, volume, speed or a servo angle.
key_facts: Three pins: the outer two go to + and GND, the middle (wiper) gives a voltage between them
Read the wiper with analogRead (0-1023 on a 5 V Arduino)
Value is printed as a code, for example B10K = 10 kOhm linear
cautions: Do not pass motor current through it - use it only as a control input
cannot_tell: Its resistance or whether it is linear or logarithmic

Trimmer-Potentiometer.name: Trimmer potentiometer (preset)
Trimmer-Potentiometer.purpose: A small potentiometer adjusted with a screwdriver to set something once - such as LCD contrast or a sensor threshold.
key_facts: Works like a rotary potentiometer: outer pins to the supply, middle pin is the wiper
Blue multi-turn trimmers need many turns from end to end
Many sensor modules use one to set their detection threshold
cautions: Turn gently with the right screwdriver - the adjuster breaks easily
cannot_tell: Its resistance value

Zener-Diode.name: Zener diode
Zener-Diode.purpose: A diode designed to conduct backwards at a fixed voltage, used as a simple voltage reference or to limit voltage.
key_facts: Connected 'backwards' (band/cathode towards +) with a series resistor
Holds the voltage near its Zener rating, for example 5.1 V
Usually a small glass body with a dark band
cautions: Always use a series resistor to limit current
Not a replacement for a proper voltage regulator under load
cannot_tell: Its Zener voltage - read the tiny print or measure it
Whether it is a Zener or an ordinary small-signal glass diode (such as 1N4148)
